root.name: Robatsch Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 d6 2. Nf3 g6 3. c4 Bg7 4. e4 Bg4

overview: Black fianchettoes with ...g6 and ...Bg7 and plays ...d6 before ...Nf6, then pins the f3 knight with ...Bg4 after White has built the pawn centre c4, d4 and e4. White enjoys space; Black aims to undermine the centre later with ...c5, ...e5 or ...Nc6 and ...Qd7. It is a hypermodern, flexible defence against many White set-ups rather than a forcing line.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with c4, d4, e4 and develop Nc3, Be2
Break the pin with h3 or Be2 and keep the space
Aim to hold the centre and attack with f4 or e5 at the right moment

black_ideas.idea: Fianchetto and wait, then strike with ...c5 or ...e5
Pin the knight with ...Bg4 to pressure d4
Develop ...Nd7 and ...Ngf6 to challenge the centre

typical_structures.structure: Pirc/Modern set-up against a broad white pawn centre
Black fianchetto against Maroczy-type or Four Pawns-style pawn structures

character.notes: Black accepts a space deficit and aims to counterattack later; not forcing, with a sound pawn structure.

soundness.notes: Playable, less common but not refuted.

structure.notes: The centre remains undecided until Black strikes with ...c5 or ...e5.

approach.notes: Seldom played by strong players, who prefer other defences to 1.d4; the Modern set-up is used more against 1.e4.

level.notes: Black needs to understand when and how to strike at the centre.

character.reason: Hypermodern, neither especially forcing nor especially hard to break down.

structure.reason: White big centre is not fixed and Black attacks it later.

approach.reason: Seldom played by strong players; could be read as standard or a system.

level.reason: Plans are conceptual, with moderate theory.

plans.reason: Black allows a centre and strikes at it with pieces and pawns.
